title: An Analysis of Self-supervised Pre-training with Dependent Samples
abstract: arXiv:2609.05031v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Self-supervised learning relies on so-called data augmentations $\phi(x)$ of unlabeled datapoints $x$ --- for example, masking random pixels in an image $x$ --- that should leave the label of $x$ invariant and are often used to learn a lower-complexity invariant subspace $\cal V$ for downstream tasks. In practice, such augmentations $\{ \phi_l(x_i) \}$ are pooled together to learn $\cal V$, despite obvious inter-dependencies between different augmentations $\phi_l(x), \phi_k(x)$ of the same datapoint $x$. However, theoretical works on the subject typically consider procedures that avoid such dependencies, and are therefore limited to operate on smaller subsets of independent data.   We show in this work that pooling augmentations together, despite inter-dependencies, is a better alternative than the baseline of partitioning the data into subsets of independent data. tldr: 该研究证明，在自监督预训练中，尽管同一数据点的不同增强之间存在相互依赖性，将它们汇集在一起学习比将数据划分为独立子集的基线方法是更好的选择。
en_tdlr: This paper demonstrates that pooling dependent augmentations together is a better alternative than partitioning data into subsets of independent data for learning invariant subspaces in self-supervised pre-training.
